'''''Palafoxia''''', or '''palafox''', is a genus of North American [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Bahieae|Bahia tribe]] within the [[Asteraceae]] (sunflower family).<ref>Lagasca y Segura, Mariano. 1816.  Genera et species plantarum Elench. Pl. 26</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40036366 Tropicos, ''Palafoxia'' Lag.]</ref>

== Description ==
The erect, slender [[Plant stem|stem]] grows {{Convert|30–60|cm}} tall, branching in the lower half and is sparsely leaved. It is glandular and hairy on the upper parts.<ref name="u">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=123680 Flora of North America Vol. 21 Page 388 ''Palafoxia'' Lagasca]</ref>

The glabrous, glandular [[leaves]] are lanceolate, {{Convert|3–20|mm|frac=8}} wide and {{Convert|4–7.5|cm|abbr=on|frac=8}} long, and are arranged alternately.<ref name="u" />

A few [[flower]] heads appear at  the end of the upper branches. The reddish to pink ray florets have three narrow lobes. They are subtended by involucral [[bract]]s.<ref name=u/>

The seed-like [[fruit]] is narrow with a [[Pappus (botany)|pappus]] of several pointed scales (giving rise to the common name 'Spanish Needles' for [[Palafoxia arida|''P. arida'']]). These plants self-sow freely.<ref name=u/>

== Taxonomy ==
The genus is named after [[José de Palafox y Melzi, Duke of Saragossa]] (1776–1847),  a Spanish captain-general in the [[Peninsular War]] against the invading armies of [[Napoleon]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2024}}

* ''[[Palafoxia texana]]'' <small>DC.</small> :Texas palafox - [[Nuevo León]], [[Coahuila]], [[Tamaulipas]], [[Nuevo León]], [[Veracruz]], [[Texas|TX]] [[Louisiana|LA]] [[Florida|FL]]

== Distribution and habitat ==
These are [[drought-tolerant]], annual [[herb]]s growing on sandy plains, dunes, deserts ([[Mojave Desert|Mojave desert]], [[Sonoran Desert|Sonoran desert]]) and rangeland, native to the United States and Mexico. ''P. callosa'' is [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in Hawaii.

== Ecology ==
They are attractive to bees, butterflies and birds and are used as food plants by the [[larva]]e of some [[Lepidoptera]] species including ''[[Schinia|Schinia niveicosta]]'', which feeds exclusively on ''P. linearis''.

== Uses ==
''Palafoxia rosea'' (Rosy palafox) has been used in [[folk medicine]] for the treatment of fever, nausea and chills.
